research_method.claude: SLR following Biolchini et al. and Kitchenham & Charters with quality assessment (QA1–QA4, 75% threshold); 5 databases; 1,223 results, first 100 per database = 484, 434 after duplicates, 85 selected, 35 above threshold
research_method.nlm: SLR; 35 primary studies out of 1,223 raw results, 434 unique papers screened, 85 candidates
research_method.value: Systematic literature review (Kitchenham & Charters; Biolchini et al. process) over 5 databases (IEEE Xplore, SpringerLink, ScienceDirect, ACM DL, Scopus); 1,223 results, first 100 per database by relevance (484), 434 after duplicate removal, 85 selected, 35 retained above a 75% quality threshold; factors classified into four dimensions (Team, Individual, Organizational, Process) adapted from Chow & Cao
research_method.note: First-100-per-database rule and QA details reported only by Claude (not contradicted).

context.claude: Academic review on agile development teams; primary studies cover industry, distributed/global teams and OSS (GitHub)
context.nlm: Academic SLR on agile software development teams; studies cover collocated, remote, distributed and global virtual teams
context.value: academic (secondary/review); 35 primary studies on agile software development teams (industry, collocated and distributed/global teams, OSS on GitHub)

remote_covid.note: Geographic/temporal distance among the most influential factors; support for remote work; COVID-19 work intensification as motivation.

cat_productivity.note: Productivity of agile teams is the synthesized outcome; indicators cited: tasks delivered on time, workload per developer ratio, team velocity.

cat_quality.note: Code quality/architecture, testability, rework and technical debt as factors and indicators.

cat_collaboration.note: Communication, interaction between members, psychological safety, teamwork quality and Kanban communication patterns are central findings.

cat_satisfaction.note: Motivation, morale and work environment appear only as influencing factors; neither extractor lists a satisfaction/well-being measure.

cat_activity.note: NotebookLM tags tasks on time, workload ratio and tenure/turnover as Activity, but none is a repository activity metric.

cat_delivery.note: Thin basis: both tag 'tasks delivered on time' (manager perspective, one primary study) as Delivery; Claude also tags team velocity as Delivery (velocity belongs to productivity per the definitions). No deploy/lead-time metric.

cat_devex.note: NotebookLM's Quality/DevEx tag on technical debt is generic; no DevEx framework.

cat_agile.note: Review of agile teams; RQ2 on adapting agile practices; iteration planning, sprint goals, Kanban, Scrum/XP practices mapped to factors.

cat_survey.note: Claude: no perceptual instrument synthesized. NotebookLM: perception surveys/questionnaires listed as collection method of several primary-study metrics (manager perceptions, TWQ, morale).

evidence.quote: this paper presents the state of the art of socio-cultural factors that influence the way agile development teams work, analyzing their impact on their productivity through a systematic literature review (SLR) process [10].

in [52] they analyze productivity indicators from the project manager's perspective, including tasks delivered on time and outputs that meet stakeholder expectations.
